# Rabbit Chain

Official website: https://rabbitchain.org
Official GitHub: https://github.com/rabbitmainnet
Official X: https://x.com/rabbit_mainnet

Rabbit Chain is a permissionless EVM Layer 1 powered by LCQ Consensus. Rabbit Testnet (Chain ID 9280) is the first public network. Rabbit Mainnet (Chain ID 928) follows validation.
Rabbit Core Testnet v2.4.15 upgrade: v2.4.15 (source commit b74320bc6e9b66894add55ff378274c4c402dd2e).
Rabbit Core v2.4.15 adds verified automatic multipart blockchain bootstrap, resumable downloads, progress reporting and wallet-first initialization for new miners. Existing miners retain their data. Earlier releases added authenticated encrypted DKG evaluations and verified VRF partial signatures through public peers when miners have no direct connection. This release schedules the Testnet fork at block 320,000. Availability V2 activated at block 173057 in v2.4.6. Any user or contract can request VRF without mining. Earlier fork heights and the existing genesis, wallets and blockchain data are preserved. Keep the operating-system clock synchronized. VRF completion must be verified through canonical request status, randomness and proof; local key creation alone is not completion.
Rabbit VRF DKG preparation started at block 136065. Rabbit VRF protocol and the VRF liveness rules activated at block 136193. Protocol activation is distinct from verified fulfillment. Public request testing is experimental: inspect canonical completion before using randomness.

Extracting software on another drive does not move the data directory. Rabbit Core supports --data-dir; existing users must stop all Rabbit processes, copy the complete data directory and verify their existing wallet before using another location.

Key routes: /testnet, /mainnet, /lcq, /platform, /developers, /docs, /security, /releases, /status.

Earlier releases preserved the Availability V2 schedule on restart; v2.4.15 adds the Testnet block 320000 schedule.

Earlier releases improved live block import and production recovery: nodes briefly wait for an incoming direct-extension block before starting recovery, and a shorter conflicting peer no longer keeps production paused. Historical fork heights and mining rewards remain unchanged; new VRF economics and WorkSeat admission activate at block 320,000.

Earlier releases isolated outgoing LCQ messages in bounded per-peer queues so a slow peer does not block delivery to other peers. It retries failed asynchronous recovery downloads and reports canonical penalties in English, including the end block and remaining blocks. Normal operational status refreshes approximately every 10 to 12 seconds.
PENALIZED reports missed assigned production turns, the canonical penalty end block and remaining blocks. It does not prove the underlying technical cause. Penalty expiry still requires synchronization and selection.

Rabbit Core v2.4.15 schedules VRF economics V2 and WorkSeat admission V2 at public Testnet block 320000. Keep existing chain data, wallets and identities. New installations retain the verified multipart bootstrap. Block target remains 10 seconds; mining rewards remain 70/30.
From activation the VRF base pricing target is US$0.005 equivalent in tRUSD, payable in tRAB using quoteRequestFee(0), plus gas. At fulfillment, 50% plus rounding goes to development allocation, 30% to validated VRF signers and 20% to the fulfillment block producer.
Two local SSD-backed tests completed 48 valid requests with three concurrent clients; early-proof verification took 0.176–1.242 seconds after observed inclusion. These local results do not establish public-network throughput, a latency SLA or consensus finality. The existing web timer tracks on-chain fulfillment.
